Full summary: Ran post-release housekeeping: archived 185 aged entries, pruned 2 orphaned graph entities; all 5 dangling warnings verified resolved by release-day work. Left 161 staleness candidates untouched — bulk archive would hit live architecture decisions (branch-gone false positives).
Decisions: Chose NOT to run twining_archive_stale on the 161 staleness candidates (score ≥0.95) — sampling showed load-bearing active decisions among them (e.g. 'SQLite is the runtime store and git is the replication transport', whose src/storage/ scope exists), likely flagged because their originating branches were deleted; a curated review pass is required before any bulk action.
Findings: Issue #39 reproduced a second time on live data: housekeeping preview reported 44 dedups / 0 archived, execute performed 0 dedups / 185 archived — pass ordering lets auto-archive absorb dedup candidates; preview counts remain non-binding. Fresh evidence for the v2.1 fix.; need: curated review of the 161 staleness candidates — the ≥0.95 scorer flags branch-gone items regardless of whether the decision is still architecturally load-bearing; consider a scorer tweak (active high-confidence decisions with existing scope paths should not hit 0.95 on branch deletion alone) as v2.1 input alongside #16.
